recognize_zh: 周邊血液中一群中型淋巴樣細胞，細胞質豐富淡藍、邊緣呈不規則毛狀突起，核圓至卵圓、染色質中等凝集，部分細胞可見單一小核仁，形態介於毛細胞與前淋巴球之間，符合毛細胞白血病變異型。
features: Low to moderate N:C ratio with abundant pale grey-blue cytoplasm
Irregular, ruffled cytoplasmic borders with fine hair-like projections
Round to oval nuclei with moderately condensed chromatin
Small but discernible single nucleolus in several cells
Background of normochromic red cells, some target-like, and scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a cluster of medium to large lymphoid cells with abundant pale blue cytoplasm and irregular, hairy cytoplasmic margins. The nuclei are round to oval with moderately condensed chromatin, and a small distinct nucleolus is visible in several cells. The combination of hairy cytoplasmic outlines with nucleolated, more condensed nuclei differs from classic hairy cell leukemia. Flow cytometry (CD11c+, CD103+, CD25-negative, CD123 weak/negative) and absence of BRAF V600E would support the diagnosis. Findings are consistent with hairy cell leukemia variant (splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukemia with prominent nucleoli).

ddx.vs: Classic hairy cells have oval or bean-shaped nuclei with homogeneous, less condensed chromatin and no conspicuous nucleolus, and are CD25+/annexin A1+ with BRAF V600E.
SMZL cells are smaller with scant cytoplasm and short polar villi rather than abundant circumferential hairy cytoplasm, and are CD103-negative.
Prolymphocytes have a prominent nucleolus but scant cytoplasm with smooth borders lacking hairy projections.
Monocytes have folded nuclei with lacy chromatin and vacuolated cytoplasm with fine granules, and are CD14+.
